correctness.rationale: Jacobian rank condition over characteristic zero gives exactly zero-sum sixth-root tuples up to free μ6 scaling. For each point the explicit affine Hessian determinant is -42^(N-2)/prod_{i<N} x_i, which is nonzero. All singularities are ordinary double points, singular set finite; dimensional intersection and Serre R1+S2 prove geometric integrality/normality. The Laurent identity S+2=(1+U)(1+V)(1+1/(UV)) derives the finite Franel-binomial formula exactly. Rationality is equivalent to all normalized sixth roots being ±1, giving binomial/2 counts and quadratic residual fields. Exact standalone checks use three independent enumeration methods in finite ranges and sample Hessian determinants; no finite-to-infinite inference.

originality.rationale: The complete all-dimensional seventh-power hyperplane singularity classification is not a consequence of Lam–Leung length existence, Looijenga Fermat periods, Chen–Xia pre-existing Franel combinatorics, or the cubic Segre special family. The new assertion connects a geometric node classification with a nontrivial exact Franel-binomial enumerator and quadratic arithmetic fields. Equivalent unpublished or differently titled classifications remain a stated risk; no uniqueness from database partition is claimed.
residual_risks: An unindexed theorem on singularities of diagonal hyperplane sections of Fermat hypersurfaces might subsume the formula in a different language.
The Franel-transform integer sequence and Eisenstein lattice walk enumeration may have independent combinatorial tabulations; no claim that these sequences are new by themselves.
Not every page of every relevant historic article was read, so a universal NOT_COVERING conclusion is not claimed.

value.rationale: A natural high-degree family of symmetric Fermat hyperplane sections is given a complete all-dimension singular-basket and arithmetic closed-point classification. Nontrivial root-of-unity six-step enumerations yield an explicit Franel-number formula and an exact rational/quadratic Galois splitting; these facts are not just a generic Jacobian criterion or re-labeling of an existing node table. The theorem is self-contained, supplies explicit numerical examples, and can support further arithmetic/geometric investigations; it does not claim extremality or positive-characteristic analogues.
